subject: Third‑party roster & supply‑chain attestations — Helix Health security review
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@helixhealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Helix Health Security Team <security@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2025-11-18T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Supply‑chain inventory + SIG/CAIQ follow up

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security team is compiling materials for our vendor intake and asked for two items to move Redwood through the next stage of review:

1) A current list of subprocessors (name, purpose, country, data category) and an indication of which subprocessors have access to customer content at rest or in transit.
2) SIG Lite / CAIQ responses or a short mapping file for the high‑risk items (encryption, data residency, key management).

Can you send a machine‑readable roster and any evidence (network segmentation diagram, SOC2 point‑in‑time date, or an attestation) by EOW? If you have an encrypted bundle or a secure link you can share, that would be preferred.

Also, two quick clarifying questions from our infosec lead: do you use any single‑tenant database providers for telemetry, and do any subprocessors handle PII beyond hashed identifiers? If you can indicate yes/no and the provider name where applicable that would help.

Best,
Emily Chen
Security Lead — Vendor Risk
Helix Health

[attachment: helix_vndr_questionnaire_v2.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@helixhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-11-18T11:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Supply‑chain inventory + SIG/CAIQ follow up

Emily —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can get this over to you; attaching a CSV export of our subprocessor roster and a short SIG‑Lite response workbook for the items you highlighted. High‑level answers to your clarifying questions below:

• Single‑tenant DB for telemetry: No — telemetry/metrics are processed in segmented projects within our cloud provider; we do not provision single‑tenant DB instances for telemetry customers.
• Subprocessors handling PII beyond hashed identifiers: Limited — our analytics vendor (DataDrift Inc.) processes user IDs and customer‑provided metadata; we mask and hash direct identifiers prior to export where required.

Next steps — Monica (CC) will assemble the network segmentation diagram and SOC2 attestation PDF. We can put everything in an encrypted folder and share a DocSend link. Will aim to send the final package by 2025‑11‑20.

Attached: redwood_subprocessors_list_20251118.csv; sig-lite-responses-helix-20251118.xlsx

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_subprocessors_list_20251118.csv (CSV); sig-lite-responses-helix-20251118.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Helix Health Security Team <security@helixhealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-11-20T08:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Supply‑chain inventory + SIG/CAIQ follow up

Hi Rishi / Redwood team —

Thanks for the quick turn. A couple of follow ups after reviewing the CSV:

1) The CSV lists 'EdgeCache Systems' as caching provider (US). Can you confirm whether caching is used for any customer content or only for model artifacts and static assets?
2) For DataDrift Inc., can you share a brief description of the controls around masking/hashing (what transforms, retention window, and whether they have SOC2)?

If you prefer, we can take a short 30‑minute call to go over these two items; our calendar shows availability 2025‑11‑21 between 10:00–12:00 PT.

Thanks — Emily on behalf of the security team

[attached: helix_obs_qs_11_20.pdf (PDF)]

From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Helix Health Security Team <security@helixhealth.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@helixhealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-11-21T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Supply‑chain inventory + SIG/CAIQ follow up

Hi Emily / Helix team —

Thanks for the review and the specific questions. Quick responses and evidence links below: 

1) EdgeCache Systems (caching): used for model artifact distribution and non‑sensitive static assets only. No customer prompt or generation content is cached there. Evidence: network segmentation diagram (attached) shows separate egress paths and ACLs.

2) DataDrift Inc. (analytics): they receive hashed identifiers + non‑PII telemetry. Controls: SHA‑256 hashing prior to transmission, 30‑day rolling retention for raw telemetry, pseudonymization process documented in their SOC2 Type II report. We have a current SOC2 summary from DataDrift and the contract clause requiring encryption at rest/in transit. Evidence files are in the secure bundle below.

Secure bundle (read‑only): https://docsend.com/view/rdwd-helix-evidence-2025 (access expires 2025‑12‑05)
Google Drive (limited view): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2BexAMPLE_shared-evidence
HubSpot record: HSP-44721

Attachments included in the bundle: redwood_network-seg-diagram.pdf; SOC2-supplier-summaries.pdf; sig-lite-responses-helix-20251120.xlsx

If you want to jump on the 30‑minute slot tomorrow, Laura can join to walk through the diagram — happy to do a screenshare. Otherwise, confirm if the DocSend bundle satisfies and we can proceed to the contract review stage.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Security Operations — Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_network-seg-diagram.pdf (PDF); SOC2-supplier-summaries.pdf (PDF); sig-lite-responses-helix-20251120.xlsx (XLSX)]
